decisions.reason: This automation product builds directly on the firm's control and process know-how, and after keeping it through 2024 the firm is likely to use its strong R&D and project-learning capacity to refine it rather than withdraw it.

The weir-dimensioning web tool fits the firm's engineering and planner-facing knowledge base, but as a narrower standalone digital tool with weaker attachment to the core integrated systems business it remains the most exposed to portfolio pruning.

The spring-controlled flap weir is close to the firm's established hydraulic infrastructure offer, so existing engineering knowledge and customer access support retention, though its newer and more niche mechanical profile leaves some withdrawal risk.

An energy management system for water facilities matches the firm's strategic direction toward digitally networked, efficient infrastructure and is exactly the kind of product its internal R&D and research partnerships can improve commercially.

The overflow flap gate product line is closely related to the firm's water-control business and its presence as a multi-model line indicates enough fit and commitment that the firm is more likely to extend and learn from it than to remove it.
